intro: Most people paste their resume into AI and say "make it better". You get generic. This chain works because each prompt builds on the last, in the same conversation, against one specific job.

free.title: Prompt 1: The match score
free.body: Copy this inAct as a senior recruiter for this role. Here's the job description: [paste] and my resume: [paste]. Score how well I match out of 100, list the top 5 missing keywords or skills, and say which of my experiences is most relevant.

free.title: Prompt 2: Close the gaps honestly
free.body: Copy this inRewrite my experience section to naturally include those keywords, but only where my experience truly supports them. If I don't have a skill, don't add it; list it separately as something to learn.

free.title: Prompt 3: Results bullets
free.body: Copy this inRewrite each bullet using this formula: Accomplished [X], as measured by [Y], by doing [Z]. Ask me for any numbers you need; don't invent them.

free.title: Prompt 4: The scanner check
free.body:
Copy this inNow act as an applicant tracking system. Scan my new resume: list what you'd read correctly, any sections or formatting you'd struggle with, and the final keyword match.

Then export with simple formatting: one column, standard headings, no tables or images.

free.title: Prompt 5: Interview prep
free.body:
Copy this inAct as the hiring manager for this role. Ask me the 3 hardest questions you'd ask this candidate, one at a time. After each answer, give me a stronger version based on my real background.

Everything on your resume should be true. AI helps you say it well; it can't make it true.
